The 25 km circle at 9.20E 52.64N (about 1,960 km2) is the one duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg uses for the 1582 gain; soft. The county was divided between Gerhard III and John II in 1345 and 'reunified' in 1497, inside one state.

ledger.note: 1202: Count Henry. Infobox 'Henry I Count of Hoya: 1202'; 'A first Count Henry at Hoya in Saxony appeared as a vassal of Archbishop Hartwig II of Bremen in 1202.'
1215: Nienburg. 'The Province of Nienburg was acquired in 1215.' (The Hodenberg estates were 'gradually acquired by Count Henry and his descendants until 1313'.)

1345: a division. 'In 1345 the brothers Gerhard III and John II of Hoya divided the county among themselves'; 'when the elder branch of the Gerhard line at Hoya became extinct in 1497, the territories were re-unified'. Entered as a dynastic step inside one state.

1582: the line dies out. 'The county was partitioned after Otto VIII, Count of Hoya died without sons in 1582'; 'absorbed into the Duchy of Brunswick-Luneburg in 1582', the majority to the Calenberg line, the rest to the Lüneburg line and Hesse-Cassel. (The Dukes of Brunswick-Lüneburg 'in 1512 occupied their estates', and in 1450 the family 'became embroiled in the Münster Diocesan Feud'.)
